Entomology.question: Ulisse Aldrovandi's De Animalibus Insectis (Concerning Insect Animals) was published in _____

Entomology.fact: Early entomological works associated with the naming and classification of species followed the practice of maintaining cabinets of curiosity, predominantly in Europe.

Entomology.subject: Agricultural Entomology

Entomology.fact: This has led to the development of automated species identification systems targeted on insects, for example, Daisy, ABIS, SPIDA and Draw-wing.

Entomology.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Entomology.question: While not true entomologists in the traditional sense, individuals who attain the ACE certification may be referred to as ACEs or _____

Entomology.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Entomology.question: As such, other credential programs managed by the _____ of America have varying credential requirements
Entomology.fact: As such, other credential programs managed by the Entomological Society of America have varying credential requirements.

Entomology.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Entomology.question: These individuals also have to "agree to ascribe to a code of ethical behavior" (ESA _____)

Entomology.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Entomology.question: As with this, they also have to fulfill a certain number of educational requirements every 12 months (ESA _____)

Insect.fact: The abdomen is the largest part of the insect, typically with 11–12 segments, and is less strongly sclerotized than the head or thorax.

Insect.fact: The colors of emitted light vary from dull blue (Orfelia fultoni, Mycetophilidae) to the familiar greens and the rare reds (Phrixothrix tiemanni, Phengodidae).

Insect.fact: Chemical defense is common among Coleoptera and Lepidoptera, usually being advertised by bright warning colors (aposematism), as in the monarch butterfly.

Insect.fact: Some ground beetles of the family Carabidae actively defend themselves, spraying chemicals from their abdomen with great accuracy, to repel predators.

Insect.fact: The largest group, with over 100,000 species and perhaps over a million, consists of a single clade of parasitoid wasps among the Hymenoptera.

Insect.fact: A larger 2020 meta-study, analyzing data from 166 long-term surveys, suggested that populations of terrestrial insects are indeed decreasing rapidly, by about 9% per decade.

Metamorphosis.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Metamorphosis.question: The _____ was Profound change in body structure during the postembryonic development of an organism.
Metamorphosis.fact: Metamorphosis is a biological process in which an animal undergoes a conspicuous and relatively abrupt change in its body structure as part of its development. Some insects, fish, amphibians, mollusks, crustaceans, cnidarians, echinoderms, and tunicates undergo metamorphosis, often accompanied by a change of nutrition or behavior.

Metamorphosis.subject: Agricultural Entomology

Metamorphosis.subject: Agricultural Entomology

Larva.question: The _____ was Juvenile form of distinct animals before metamorphosis.

Pollinator.subject: Agricultural Entomology
Pollinator.question: The _____ was Animal that moves pollen from the male anther of a flower to the female stigma.
Pollinator.fact: A pollinator is an animal that moves pollen from the male anther of a flower to the female stigma of a flower. Insects are the major pollinators of most plants, and insect pollinators include all families of bees and most families of aculeate wasps; ants; many families of flies; many lepidopterans (both butterflies and moths); and many families of beetles.
